name: Dum Aloo
cuisine: North Indian (Punjabi restaurant style; the dish began in Kashmiri Pandit cooking)

ingredients.name: Sunflower oil (or other neutral oil)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2½ tsp (1½ tsp to fry the potatoes + 1 tsp for the gravy)

ingredients.name: Onion (pyaz/kanda)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ small onion, finely chopped (about ⅓ cup)

ingredients.name: Tomato (tamatar)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 small-medium ripe tomato, pureed with the cashews

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.householdMeasure: a little under ½ cup (plus water for boiling the potatoes, not counted)

equipment: Pressure cooker (small) or a saucepan with a lid, to boil the potatoes
Kadai or medium heavy pan with a tight lid (about 20 cm)
Mixer-grinder (small chutney jar) for the tomato-cashew puree
Toothpick, fork or skewer, to prick the potatoes so the gravy soaks in
Mortar and pestle (khalbatta) or grater for the ginger and garlic
Small bowl and spoon or whisk, to beat the curd
Wooden spoon or spatula, measuring spoons and a measuring cup (a normal teaspoon and a steel glass work)
Optional: a flat tawa under the kadai during dum, so the bottom does not burn

steps.title: Wash the potatoes
steps.text: Rinse 150 g baby potatoes (6–8) under running water and rub off any soil.
steps.visualCue: Clean skins, no mud in the eyes
steps.cameraCheck: The washed potatoes in a bowl
steps.videoShot: Baby potatoes rubbed clean under the tap.

steps.title: Boil the potatoes
steps.text: Put them in the pressure cooker with water just to cover and a pinch of salt. Cook for 1 whistle on medium-high, then 2 min on low, and turn off. (Saucepan: boil covered for 12–15 min.)
steps.tip: Do not overcook. The potatoes cook again in the gravy, and soft ones fall apart (Hebbar's Kitchen gives the same warning).
steps.visualCue: A knife tip goes in with a little resistance at the centre, so they are about 90% done
steps.videoShot: Steam hissing from the cooker whistle.

steps.title: Peel the potatoes
steps.text: Drain them, let them cool for 2–3 min, then slip off the skins with your fingers.
steps.tip: Very thin, clean skins can be left on for extra fibre.
steps.visualCue: Smooth, pale-yellow potatoes, whole and unbroken
steps.cameraCheck: The peeled potatoes on a plate
steps.videoShot: Skin pulled off a warm baby potato.

steps.title: Prick the potatoes
steps.text: Prick each potato 5–6 times all over with a toothpick or fork.
steps.tip: The holes let the gravy soak into the centre.
steps.visualCue: Small holes all around each potato
steps.videoShot: A fork pricking a potato on all sides.

steps.title: Make the tomato-cashew puree
steps.text: Blend 80 g roughly chopped tomato with 4 cashews (6 g) and 1 tbsp water until smooth.
steps.visualCue: A smooth, light-orange puree with no cashew bits
steps.videoShot: The mixer jar spinning, then the puree poured out.

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Finely chop ½ small onion (50 g).
steps.visualCue: Small, even pieces, about ⅓ cup
steps.videoShot: Knife chopping onion finely.

steps.title: Crush the ginger and garlic
steps.text: Crush or grate ½-inch ginger (3 g) and 2 small garlic cloves (4 g) to a coarse paste.
steps.visualCue: Coarse paste with a strong smell
steps.videoShot: Ginger and garlic pounded in a khalbatta.

steps.title: Whisk the curd
steps.text: Whisk 40 g (2½ tbsp) curd with ¾ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, ¾ tsp coriander powder and a pinch of turmeric until smooth.
steps.tip: Mixing the powders into the curd first helps stop the curd splitting in the pan, and the powders cannot burn.
steps.visualCue: Smooth, orange-pink curd with no lumps
steps.cameraCheck: The spiced curd in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Spoon whisking spices into curd.

steps.title: Heat oil for the potatoes
steps.text: Heat 1½ tsp (7 g) oil in the kadai on medium.
steps.visualCue: Oil shimmers
steps.videoShot: Oil swirled in a hot kadai.

steps.title: Shallow-fry the potatoes
steps.text: Add the pricked potatoes in one layer and fry, turning every minute.
steps.tip: Keep a lid half on; boiled potatoes can spit when they hit oil.
steps.visualCue: Golden-brown, lightly crisp skin on all sides
steps.cameraCheck: The golden potatoes in the pan
steps.videoShot: Potatoes rolled in the kadai as they turn golden.

steps.title: Take out the potatoes
steps.text: Lift the potatoes out onto a plate, leaving the oil in the kadai.
steps.visualCue: A thin film of oil left in the pan
steps.cameraCheck: The fried potatoes on the plate
steps.videoShot: Potatoes lifted out with a slotted spoon.

steps.title: Add the gravy oil and whole spices
steps.text: Add 1 tsp (5 g) more oil to the kadai, then ¼ tsp cumin seeds, 1 bay leaf, 1 cracked cardamom, 1 clove and the ½-inch cinnamon.
steps.tip: If the cumin turns black at once, the oil is too hot; lower the heat.
steps.visualCue: Cumin sizzles and darkens one shade; warm spice smell
steps.videoShot: Whole spices crackling in oil.

steps.title: Cook the onion
steps.text: Add the onion and stir often on medium heat.
steps.visualCue: Soft and golden at the edges, sweet smell
steps.videoShot: Onion stirred as it turns golden.

steps.title: Add the ginger and garlic
steps.text: Add the ginger-garlic paste and stir.
steps.visualCue: Raw garlic smell gone
steps.videoShot: Paste stirred into the onion.

steps.title: Cook the tomato-cashew puree
steps.text: Pour in the puree and add ¼ tsp (1.5 g) salt. Cook on medium, stirring.
steps.visualCue: The puree thickens, darkens to deep orange and oil shows at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: Oil at the edge of the masala
steps.videoShot: Spoon dragging through thick masala.

steps.title: Cool the pan for the curd
steps.text: Turn the heat to the lowest setting and wait 30 seconds.
steps.visualCue: The masala stops bubbling hard
steps.videoShot: The flame turned down.

steps.title: Add the curd
steps.text: Add the spiced curd and stir without stopping.
steps.tip: White specks mean the curd split; it still tastes fine, and you can blend the gravy smooth if you mind how it looks.
steps.visualCue: The gravy turns smooth and orange with no white specks
steps.videoShot: Curd poured in and stirred fast.

steps.title: Cook the curd masala
steps.text: Raise the heat to medium and cook, stirring.
steps.visualCue: Oil separates again at the edges
steps.videoShot: Gravy bubbling gently with oil at the edge.

steps.title: Add water and potatoes
steps.text: Add 100 ml water and stir, then add the fried potatoes and turn them to coat.
steps.visualCue: Potatoes coated in a pourable orange gravy
steps.videoShot: Potatoes slid into the gravy.

steps.title: Cook on dum
steps.text: Cover tightly and simmer on the lowest heat (on a tawa if you have one), stirring gently once halfway.
steps.tip: If the gravy sticks, add 2 tbsp hot water.
steps.visualCue: Gravy thick and clinging, a thin layer of oil on top, potatoes soft to the centre
steps.cameraCheck: The pan with the lid lifted
steps.videoShot: Lid lifted, steam rising off glossy potatoes.

steps.title: Finish with garam masala and kasuri methi
steps.text: Sprinkle ¼ tsp garam masala and crush ½ tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the pan. Stir and turn off the heat.
steps.visualCue: Green flecks, warm smell
steps.cameraCheck: The kasuri methi on the curry
steps.videoShot: Palms rubbing kasuri methi over the pan.

steps.title: Taste and adjust
steps.text: Taste; add a pinch of salt only if needed, or 2 tbsp hot water for a looser gravy.
steps.visualCue: Rich, mildly spicy, gently tangy from curd and tomato
steps.videoShot: A spoonful lifted for tasting.

steps.title: Garnish and serve
steps.text: Remove the bay leaf and cinnamon, transfer to a bowl and scatter 1 tsp chopped coriander leaves on top.
steps.visualCue: Golden potatoes in a thick orange-red gravy
steps.videoShot: Coriander scattered over the bowl, steam rising.

reasons: potatoes give potassium, vitamin B6 and some fibre, the potatoes are shallow-fried rather than deep-fried, and the gravy uses curd and a few cashews instead of cream, so saturated fat stays low (about 2.5 g) at about 340 kcal. Points off because it is mostly starch with only about 7.5 g protein, about 16 g fat from frying, and moderate sodium (about 825 mg). Restaurant versions usually deep-fry the potatoes and finish with cream and butter, so 450–600 kcal bowls with 10 g or more saturated fat are common.

researchRating.basis: a well-loved North Indian party and restaurant curry: Hebbar's Kitchen's Punjabi dhaba-style dum aloo shows 4.99 from about 259 votes, Tarla Dalal's restaurant-style Punjabi dum aloo 4.9 from 61 reviews, and Veg Recipes of India's Kashmiri dum aloo has at least 3 pages of comments. Every major Indian recipe site (Indian Healthy Recipes, Whisk Affair, Sanjeev Kapoor, Cook with Manali, Yummy Tummy) publishes it, and Wikipedia notes it is cooked widely across India and Pakistan. Points off because it is rich and fried, is seen as a special-occasion dish rather than an everyday one, and there is confusion between the Kashmiri and Punjabi styles. Platform dish ratings were not used.

storage: Fridge-safe in a closed box for up to 2 days (cool within 1 hour). Freezing is not recommended: the potatoes turn grainy and the curd gravy can split on thawing. Reheat in a pan on low with 2–3 tbsp water, stirring gently, until it bubbles; or microwave covered in 1-minute bursts. The gravy thickens overnight, so loosen it with water.
leftoverRemix: Dum aloo kathi roll. Lift out the potatoes, halve them and cook the leftover gravy down until it is very thick. Toss the potatoes back in with a pinch of chaat masala, then roll them in a warm roti brushed with green chutney, add sliced onion and a squeeze of lemon, and toast the roll on a tawa with ½ tsp oil.
burnOff: about 4.9 km of running (340 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 6.8 km of brisk walking (about 1 h 20 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With 2 phulkas (about 520 kcal): about 7.4 km running or 10.4 km walking (est.).

navratri.reason: potato is allowed, but onion, garlic, coriander powder and table salt are not under the common rule set; cook the Sattvik (Kashmiri) variant with sendha namak and leave out the hing. Veg Recipes of India notes the no-onion-no-garlic Kashmiri version can be made for vrat. Family rules on turmeric and chilli vary.

ekadashi.reason: no grains or pulses in the dish, so potato is fine; use the Sattvik (Kashmiri) variant without onion and garlic, with sendha namak (common rule set).

jain.reason: potato is the main ingredient, and onion, garlic and fresh ginger are root vegetables too.

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so there is no halal-meat issue; it is a filling curry with roti for iftar dinner. Salt is moderate (about 825 mg sodium) and the dish is quite rich, so keep the portion small at sehri.

jain.reason: potato is the base of the dish, and the gravy also uses onion, garlic and fresh ginger, which are root vegetables; without the potato it is a different dish.

vegan.reason: the only animal product is 40 g curd; use the Vegan variant (extra cashew and lemon juice instead of curd).

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, no meat, so it fits a pescatarian diet.

sattvik.reason: cook the Kashmiri-style Sattvik variant (no onion, garlic or tomato; curd, fennel and dry ginger gravy).

glutenFree.reason: no wheat, maida, rava or besan, and the main recipe uses no hing; check the garam masala label for added flour. If you add hing, use a gluten-free one, because most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour.

dairyFree.reason: the dairy is 40 g curd (dahi); use the Dairy-free variant. Restaurant versions often add cream or butter as well.
